guard.disposition.log_only.label: Just do it, log only
guard.disposition.log_only.headline: Allowed
guard.disposition.notify_after.label: Do it, then tell me
guard.disposition.notify_after.headline: Allowed
guard.disposition.notify_after.nextStep: Go ahead; the user is told once it's done.
guard.disposition.plan_listed.label: Only if in the plan
guard.disposition.ask_first.label: Ask me first
guard.disposition.ask_first.headline: Ask the user first
guard.disposition.ask_first.nextStep: The daemon asks the user to approve it and runs it only once approved; don't work around it another way.
guard.disposition.hand_over.label: Hand it to me
guard.disposition.hand_over.headline: Hand it to the user
guard.disposition.hand_over.nextStep: Don't run it yourself: gather what's needed and hand it to the user to do by hand.
guard.disposition.never.label: Never
guard.disposition.never.headline: Never
guard.disposition.never.nextStep: This call won't run, and no setting, grant or user approval can loosen that; try another way or drop this step.
guard.categories.external_send: Sending or publishing in my name
guard.categories.delete_or_overwrite: Deleting or overwriting (in project records and working folders)
guard.categories.account_security: Accounts and security (credentials, permissions, global installs)
guard.categories.memory_out_of_scope: Using memory outside the granted scope
guard.bottomLines.payment_account_auth: Payments and transfers, creating accounts, changing passwords or two-step verification
guard.watch.bottomLineFixed: "{title}" is a bottom line, fixed at "{disposition}"; it can't be changed
guard.watch.onlyStricter: "{title}" can only be made stricter: "{disposition}" is looser than the default "{fallback}"
guard.watch.file.notObject: Watch category settings must be an object
guard.watch.file.badScene: builtin.{id}.{scene}: the only scenes are chat and task
guard.watch.file.onlyStricter: builtin.{id}.{scene}: built-in categories can only be made stricter; {disposition} is looser than the default {fallback}
guard.watch.file.matchList: {where}.match.{key} must be a non-empty array of strings
guard.watch.store.badJson: Watch category settings {file} isn't valid JSON: {error}
guard.tools.git_rewrite: Rewrite git history or change branches and tags
guard.tools.network_read: Read-only network command (ping, looking things up on GitHub…)
guard.tools.run_package: Download and run package (npx and the like)
guard.secrets.url_credentials: Password or token in a URL
guard.secrets.assigned_secret: Password or key in an assignment
guard.secrets.readValue: a value from a secret file read earlier
guard.ownApiNote: sent to Ergo's own API (local port {ports}), so the local exception doesn't apply
guard.paths.variable: the path has a variable or command substitution, or is under a folder that can't be determined
guard.paths.cdUnknown: an earlier cd went to a folder that can't be determined
guard.paths.fileUrl: a file:// address that can't be parsed
guard.paths.homeUnknown: the home folder can't be determined
guard.paths.driveRoot: a path under a Git Bash mount point or the current drive's root
guard.templates.backupBeforeOverwrite.ti: Back up or git-commit files in project records and working folders before deleting or overwriting them
guard.templates.backupBeforeOverwrite.me: "{p.path}" has no git commit and no backup. Commit it first (git_commit) or copy a backup (cp), then delete or overwrite it; to change only part of an existing file, use edit.
guard.templates.testBeforePush.title: Run tests before pushing
guard.templates.testBeforePush.message: Tests must pass in this repo before pushing. Run them first (run_tests, or npm test in bash), then push once they pass.
guard.templates.testBeforePush.repair: Run the tests in this repo before pushing
guard.templates.noSendAfterSecretRead.ti: Nothing goes out after reading .env or secret files
guard.templates.noSendAfterSecretRead.me: A .env or secret file was read earlier, so nothing may be sent out from here on (non-GET requests, requests with data or uploads, messages, pushes, publishing, creating remote repos, scripts using network libraries, and network commands that take piped input or have $(…) or variables in their arguments). This step can't be done. Pulling things down (read-only GET, downloads, installing dependencies, git pull / clone) is still fine; if something really has to go out, ask the user to do it.
guard.templates.noDuplicateSend.title: Don't send the same content to the same recipient twice
guard.templates.noDuplicateSend.message: The exact same content was already sent to this recipient ({current.recipients}); sending it again needs the user's confirmation
guard.templates.noSecretInOutbound.title: No secrets in outgoing content
guard.templates.noSecretInOutbound.messa: The content to be sent contains secrets ({current.secrets}). Take them out before sending; where credentials are needed, ask the user to set them up.
guard.templates.noForcePushOrRmRfOutside: No force pushes and no rm -rf outside the project

Force pushes and recursive deletes outside project records and working folders (the scratch area, for the secretary) are never allowed. Push without force; ask the user to delete things outside the project.
guard.review.timeout: The review went over its {budget} ms budget
guard.judge.secretaryAsksNote: an especially sensitive action for the secretary, so it needs your approval even with chat approvals off
guard.judge.nearBottomLineNote: the guard can't tell for sure and it might touch a protected area or secrets, so it still asks even with chat approvals off
guard.judge.beyondGrantNote: the task agent is beyond its grant; let through for now and flagged as usual
guard.judge.approvalsOffNote: chat approvals are off, so it just runs
guard.judge.secretReadOpaque: a .env or secret file was read earlier, and this command can't be seen through, so it might send secrets out
guard.judge.words.scratchAndRecords: the scratch area and project records
guard.judge.words.secretaryFence: the secretary's file tools can only write to the scratch area (project records are read-only for the secretary). Write in the scratch area; to change files in a project or elsewhere, suggest starting a task
guard.judge.words.secretaryNetworkOff: but the secretary's network switch is off. To go online, start a task (or give the user a "suggest a task" card)
guard.judge.words.projectFence: it's outside project records and working folders: a {who}'s file tools can only write to project records and working folders, and writes beyond them are always refused. Write to the working folder instead
guard.judge.words.toolkitNetworkOff: but the toolkit's network switch is off. To go online, start a task or request a toolkit change that turns networking on
guard.judge.areas.history: the project records' history area: old versions kept automatically, written only by the runtime
guard.judge.protectedArea: {how}, which is in a protected area ({area}); no agent may ever write there by any means, not even with the user's approval
guard.judge.noBash: bash isn't enabled in the toolkit
guard.judge.notInToolkit: the toolkit doesn't include the tool {tool}
guard.judge.unregistered: tool {tool} isn't registered, so there's no telling what it does
guard.judge.typedShellNoBash: {what} is a bash tool, and bash isn't enabled in the toolkit
guard.judge.unknownScopeWrite: can't confirm it's inside {scope}, or that it's outside the protected areas
guard.judge.unknownPath: the path {path} in {what} can't be determined ({why}); {scope}
guard.judge.unknownReplace: {what} would delete or overwrite {path}, which can't be determined
guard.judge.historyInside: {how}, which contains a protected area ({area} {dir}); no agent may ever write or delete there by any means, not even with the user's approval
guard.judge.secretsArea: {what} would {verb} {target}, which is in the data folder's secrets area; even reading there is refused
guard.judge.subAgentRecords: {what} would {verb} {target}: sub-agents can't write project records. Write the results to the working folder and hand them back to the maintainer
guard.judge.gitControl: {what} would {verb} {target}: that's git config or a hook, which git runs commands from, so it counts as going outside {scope}
guard.judge.writeOutsideScratch: {what} would write {target}, outside the scratch area
guard.judge.mayOverwrite: possibly overwrite {path} (not known whether it exists)
guard.judge.dataDirMention: {what} mentions a path in the data folder; it's unclear what it reads, writes or touches, so it's treated as a command that can't be split and the user is asked first
guard.judge.scriptSecrets: {how}, which is in a protected area ({area}); it's unclear whether it reads or writes, and even reading the secrets area is refused: never, not even with the user's approval
guard.judge.scriptProtected: {how}, which is in a protected area ({area}); it's unclear whether it reads or writes, so it's treated as a command that can't be split and the user is asked first
guard.judge.outsideScratch: {what} mentions paths outside the scratch area ({paths}); it's unclear what it reads or writes
guard.judge.looksLikeSend: {what} looks like it sends something out (a non-GET request or an email)
guard.judge.wildcard: {path} in {what} has a wildcard that can't be expanded (the part before the wildcard is {prefix})
guard.judge.wildcardSecrets: {how}; the wildcard can match into the data folder's secrets area, and even reading there is refused
guard.judge.wildcardProtected: {how}; it overlaps a protected area ({areas}) and might {verb}, so the user is asked first
guard.judge.httpMethod: {what} is a {method} request, not a read-only GET
guard.judge.ownPage: {what} opens Ergo's own page in a browser
guard.judge.scriptMissing: the script {what} would run doesn't exist or can't be read at check time ({path}), so it can't be checked for network use before running. Write the script with write first, then run it so it can be checked beforehand
guard.judge.scriptUnknownPath: the path {path} of the script {what} would run can't be determined, so it can't be checked for network use before running. Write the script with write first, then run it so it can be checked beforehand
guard.judge.scriptNetwork: the script {what} would run uses network libraries or functions ({usage}), {networkOff}
guard.judge.bottomLine: {what} falls under "{title}", a bottom line fixed at "{disposition}"
guard.judge.secretOutbound: the content {what} would send contains {found}; putting credentials in outgoing content is a bottom line, fixed at "Never"
guard.judge.customHit: {what} hits the custom watch category "{title}", set to "{disposition}" {where}
guard.judge.notify: the user is told when {what} is done
guard.judge.categoryHit: {reason}, which falls in the watch category "{title}" ("{disposition}" {scene})
guard.judge.noPlanInChat: chats have no plan, so it's treated as Ask me first
guard.judge.exceedsGrant: {reasons}: beyond the grant, so the user is asked first
guard.judge.unanticipated: {reasons}: the plan didn't anticipate this kind of action (it has no grant for this category), so the user is asked first and this branch stops to wait
guard.judge.otherStage: the grant {grant} for this step belongs to stage {stage}, but the current stage is {current}: grants only apply in their own stage, so it isn't allowed under that grant. Finish the current stage {current} first (declare it complete and pass review), then do this step in stage {stage}
guard.judge.neverObject: {objects}, the target of {what}, was judged "Never" earlier in this task, so outward actions on it need the user's say first
guard.judge.explain.shellNote: (generic bash: split up and judged piece by piece; each piece is shown separately on the timeline)
guard.judge.explain.refused: Refused: {text}. This call won't run, the user isn't asked, and no approval or grant can change that.{also}{shell}
guard.judge.explain.pulledBack: Sent back: {text}. This call won't run and the user isn't asked: meet the precondition as described, then call again.{also}{shell}
guard.grants.noGrant: no grant in the plan covers it
guard.grants.notThisStage: isn't for the current stage (it's for {stage}; the current one is {current})
guard.grants.onlyCommand: only allows calls split from the command "{command}"
guard.grants.exactShell: only allows calling {tool} directly; the same kind of call split from generic bash doesn't count
guard.grants.emptyArg: {param} is empty (for many tools, empty means everything)
guard.grants.extraArgs: has extra arguments not in the step: {args}
guard.grants.noRealPath: {param} is {value}, and its real path can't be determined
guard.grants.realPathOutside: the real path of {param} is {real}; allowed: {allowed}
guard.grants.change.added: added grant {grant}: while running, grants can only be narrowed; widening them means asking the user again
guard.grants.change.tool: changed the action type from {from} to {to}
guard.grants.change.realScopeWider: added {value} to the real-path scope of {param}
guard.grants.change.uses: changed the number of uses from {from} to {to}
guard.grants.change.grantedLater: moved the grant time later (earlier uses would no longer count)
guard.rules.invalid: {what}: temporal rule "{title}" failed validation ({problems}), so it can't be judged and the user is asked first
guard.rules.failed: {what}: temporal rule "{title}" errored ({error}), so it can't be judged and the user is asked first
guard.rules.unknown: {what}: temporal rule "{title}" can't be judged (a needed fact is missing, or a value the arguments or rule need can't be obtained), so the user is asked first
guard.rules.digested: {what}: temporal rule "{title}" needs content written earlier, but the effect log keeps only its length and hash, not the text, so it can't be judged and the user is asked first
guard.rules.formBefore: {tools} hasn't been done successfully yet; do it first, then come back
guard.rules.formNotBefore: {tools} was already done, so this step can't be done now
guard.planguard.forbidden: this target was explicitly excluded from the plan at review
guard.planguard.outOfScope: the arguments of {tool} go beyond the scope declared in the plan
guard.planguard.outOfOrder: {missing}, which step {step} depends on, hasn't run yet
guard.planMonitor.missingPrerequisite: A prerequisite step is missing: have the maintainer do "{title}" first, then come back to this step
guard.planMonitor.rewritten: The arguments didn't match the plan and were set back to it: {changes}
guard.shell.variableCommand: the command name {name} is a variable or command substitution, so what runs can't be determined
guard.shell.awkSystem: the awk program calls an external command
guard.shell.sedExec: the sed script has an e that runs shell commands
guard.shell.gitConfigFlag: git -c {kv} sets a config value that runs as a command
guard.shell.gitConfigSet: git config sets {key}, a config value that runs as a command
guard.shell.stdinScript: {program} reads its script from standard input
guard.shell.stdinScriptFed: {program} reads its script from standard input (fed by a pipe, here-doc or redirect)
guard.shell.remoteScript: {program} would run a script straight from the web: {url}
guard.shell.encodedCommand: {program} runs an inline or encoded command
guard.shell.always.wsl: the guard can't see commands run inside WSL
guard.shell.always.certutil: certutil can download and decode files
guard.shell.always.rundll32: it calls functions in a DLL directly
guard.shell.always.eval: eval runs a string as a command
guard.shell.always.watch: it joins its arguments into a command string and runs that
guard.shell.always.parallel: the commands it runs are strings
guard.shell.always.open: it opens things with the default program
guard.shell.denoEval: deno eval runs an inline script
guard.shell.envSplit: env -S splits a string into a command and runs it
guard.shell.trap: the command in trap is a string
guard.shell.alias: the command an alias defines is a string
guard.shell.loopCwd: a folder cd'd into repeatedly in a loop
guard.shell.recursiveCwd: a folder inside the recursive function {name}
guard.shell.badSubstitution: command substitution that can't be parsed: {text}
